title: No disk encryption policy
when: !Facts.EndpointSecurityPolicies.Any(p => p.Category == 'DiskEncryption') && !Facts.LegacyIntents.Any(p => p.Category == 'DiskEncryption') && !Facts.Derived.EncryptionPolicies.Any(p => p.RequireDeviceEncryption == true) && !Facts.ConfigurationProfiles.Any(p => p.OmaSettings.Any(o => MatchName(o.Uri, '*/BitLocker/RequireDeviceEncryption')))

messages.businessImpact: Nothing is configuring BitLocker. Whether a device is encrypted depends on how it was built, so a lost laptop may or may not be a reportable data breach and nobody can say which.
remediation: Create a BitLocker policy under Endpoint security, Disk encryption.
Enable silent encryption and escrow recovery keys to Entra ID.
messages.cannotSee: An endpoint security disk encryption policy or a classified legacy intent counts by existing, and so does a Settings Catalog profile, a security baseline or an Endpoint Protection template profile that requires device encryption, or a custom profile naming the RequireDeviceEncryption OMA-URI, whose value is not read. Whether any of them is assigned or works is not checked here; SEC-033 checks assignment for endpoint security policies. A legacy intent is classified from its template subtype; its settings and assignment targets are not read. If legacy intents or their templates cannot be read or classified, this absence check is skipped.
